thread:
incident-bot: 🚨 PAGED: p99 latency spike detected for customer Stratus (us-west-2). PagerDuty: P1. Auto-escalation: oncall-amber

oncall-amber: Saw the page. p99 ~ 7.9s right now, p95 ~ 420ms. Streaming stalls showing up as websocket disconnects. Starting triage.

sam: I can join — pulling Grafana & traces. Do we have an obvious start time?

oncall-amber: Spike started ~ 2491999800 according to metrics, ramped up at 2492000000. Affected: single-tenant cluster for Stratus (dedicated pool).

maria: Replays from the streaming tier show many sessions stuck at "response_chunk" state for >4s, then clients close. Logs show repeated KV cache misses for long prefixes.

ben: grabbing kube logs for the serving pods: `kubectl -n redwood logs svc/stratus-serving --since=10m`

ben: pasted sample error block: ```
W [2026-03-15T14:00:12Z] kvcache: miss for prefix id=0x9f4a
I [2026-03-15T14:00:12Z] rt: dispatch request id=... seq=1
E [2026-03-15T14:00:15Z] stream: stall detected, write timeout
```

kai: Are these requests unusually long? Might be prompt length + system messages. Customer said they pushed a large prompt batch earlier today.

oncall-amber: Confirmed. Stratus telemetry shows a spike in median prompt token length from ~120 -> ~3.2k for a subset of sessions around the same time.

sam: That explains KV cache churn. Long prefixes cause cache entries to be large and eviction churn increases latency for subsequent requests. Combined with ~3x concurrency spike this looks like cache thrash + backpressure.

oncall-amber: Service is Dedicated (pinned GPU pool) — capacity should be stable but concurrency burst may have exceeded intended per-pod sockets.

maria: Checking runtime batching metrics: continuous_batching drops from 0.8 to 0.2 for those pods, meaning batching broke down into many small, slow streams.

nicole: Customer impact: Stratus reported 18% of streaming sessions experienced stalls or disconnects in last 10m. Support page open.

ben: Trying immediate mitigation: toggling per-connection concurrency cap on the ingress for that tenant to 2 active streams per connection. Command: `redwoodctl tenancy update --tenant stratus --conn-max-streams 2`

oncall-amber: Apply it. We'll see if it reduces contention.

incident-bot: action taken by ben at 2492000078: `conn-max-streams` set to 2 for tenant stratus.

sam: Also enabling fallback routing for streaming to model-compact-v1 for new sessions. This keeps throughput but cheaper/smaller model should reduce KV working set. `routing: tenant=stratus -> model-compact-v1 (canary)`

oncall-amber: Can we avoid hurting quality? We should only route new sessions and not roll existing ones.

maria: Canary rule in place: route <=20% new sessions. Pushing now.

ben: Monitoring... p99 drops to 4.2s after conn cap and 20% canary. p95 ~ 360ms. Still elevated but trending down.

kai: Good. Also recommend enabling prefix-level caching TTL bump for this tenant: `kvcache.ttl=30m` (was 5m). That will reduce re-fetch pressure for longer prefixes. Are we comfortable with memory increase?

oncall-amber: Memory headroom exists on these pods (roughly 30% free). Do it as temporary mitigation.

incident-bot: action taken by maria at 2492000150: `kvcache.ttl` set to 30m for tenant stratus.

ben: After TTL bump and conn cap, p99 now ~1.6s, p95 ~320ms. Streaming disconnect rate down to 3%. Customer support notified with a mitigation note.

nicole: I've sent the customer an initial update: "We've applied temporary throttling and routing mitigations and are investigating the root cause. We'll follow up with a timeline and post-incident summary."

sam: Next steps for root cause: 1) pull a representative trace for a stalled request, 2) collect KV cache hit/miss heatmap per-prefix length, 3) examine whether the customer's recent change introduced repeated long-prefix churn (e.g., server-side prompt stitching).

kai: Also capture `perf` and `nvprof` samples on the serving pods to ensure it's not an unexpected kernel slowdown or PCIe saturation.

oncall-amber: Assigning tasks: sam -> traces & heatmap, ben -> perf sampling + pod-level metrics, maria -> routing + cache config audit. I'll own the customer comms and on-call coordination.

ben: Running `kubectl exec` and `rd-ops collect-perf --pod stratus-serve-0 --duration 60s` now.

sam: Found a trace: large prompt causes repeated KV lookups across prefixes, each lookup triggers RPC to the model shard due to cache miss, serialization of KV access adds ~200ms per lookup. For requests with ~50k token-equivalent prefix processing, that sums to seconds.

maria: On routing audit: There was an automated config rollout earlier today (09:40) from Stratus onboarding flow that increased per-session context assembly and turned on a "client-side stitching" feature. Might be the trigger.

nicole: Support confirms Stratus started a new feature flag for long-document stitching at 09:35. They didn't expect it to be live at scale.

oncall-amber: That is our probable root cause: customer feature increased prefix sizes and concurrency spike amplified KV cache thrash -> streaming stalls. Mitigations applied.

sam: Recommended medium-term fixes: 1) add prefix size guards (reject or chunk large client prompts), 2) improve KV cache eviction policy to favor recent prefixes, 3) increase async prefetch for long prefix sequences, 4) tenant-specific rate limits for new features.

oncall-amber: For now we'll keep conn cap and TTL bump. Schedule a maintenance window with Stratus to test a config that chunks their stitching into smaller segments.

ben: Metrics look stable. p99 holding ~1.5s for last 5m. No regression to >4s.

maria: I'll prepare an incident summary draft with timeline, mitigations, root cause hypothesis, and follow-ups.

nicole: Support note updated and Stratus ops on call for post-mortem at 16:00 PT.

oncall-amber: Handoff: I'm going to sleep but leaving in Sam's hands for follow-ups. Sam, you're primary until postmortem.

sam: Taking over. Will complete data collection and join the PM call.

incident-bot: Incident P1 -> acknowledged by sam at 2492000360. Incident pinned.

oncall-amber: Thanks everyone. If anything regresses escalate immediately. :thumbsup:

sam: Will file the follow-up ticket: `INC-2492` with action items: monitoring alerts for prefix-length spikes, tenant-specific conn caps by default, KV cache tuning knobs exposed in console.

maria: Attaching relevant query snippets in the postmortem doc: `SELECT prefix_len, count(1), avg(latency) FROM kv_access WHERE tenant='stratus' GROUP BY prefix_len`

ben: Leaving logs and perf artifacts in /mnt/incidents/2492000000/ for the postmortem.

nicole: Closing support incident after follow-up call unless Stratus requests more.

sam: Closing thread for now — monitoring continues.

oncall-amber: logged. Good work team.
